hook.text: Nikola claimed to have a working hydrogen truck. The demo video used a truck rolling downhill.

buildup.text: The EV startup went public via SPAC and reached a $30 billion valuation without selling a truck.

discovery.text: A short seller proved the demo truck was unpowered—just gravity doing the work.

twist.text: Founder Trevor Milton made false claims about technology, partnerships, and revenue.

climax.text: Milton was convicted of fraud in 2022 and sentenced to four years in prison.

punchline.text: The truck didn't drive. It just rolled downhill.

quiz.question: What did a short seller prove about Nikola's truck demo?
options: The truck was rolling downhill under gravity
It was a different brand's truck

details.summary: Nikola Motors claimed to have revolutionary hydrogen-powered semi-truck technology, but founder Trevor Milton fabricated demonstrations and misrepresented the company's capabilities. This topic covers the deception, including the infamous rolling truck video, and the securities fraud conviction.
details.whyItMatters: Nikola shows that accounting fraud extends beyond financial statements. Misrepresenting technological capabilities to inflate stock price is a form of securities fraud with massive investor consequences.
takeaways: Nikola's promotional video of a 'working' truck was actually the vehicle rolling downhill with no engine power
The company claimed proprietary technology it did not actually possess
Founder Trevor Milton was convicted of securities fraud and wire fraud in 2022

faq.question: What did Nikola Motors lie about?
faq.answer: Nikola's founder Trevor Milton falsely claimed the company had built a working hydrogen truck and showed a promotional video of it driving. In reality, the truck was unpowered and simply rolled downhill. He also lied about having proprietary battery and hydrogen technology.

faq.question: How was the Nikola fraud exposed?
faq.answer: Short seller Hindenburg Research published a detailed report titled 'Nikola: How to Parlay an Ocean of Lies into a Partnership with the Largest Auto OEM in America,' revealing that the truck video was staged and technology claims were fabricated. Federal prosecutors then investigated.
